title: Class II Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC)

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: A ventilated enclosure using HEPA-filtered, directional airflow to protect the worker, the environment, and (depending on cabinet type) the product/sample from exposure to aerosolized biological material.
operatingPrinciple: Room air is drawn inward across the work surface (protecting the worker), and HEPA-filtered air moves downward over the work area; exhaust air also passes through a HEPA filter before leaving the cabinet or being recirculated, depending on the specific cabinet type.
basicOperation: Allow the cabinet blower to run and airflow to stabilize for the manufacturer-specified warm-up time before starting work.
Avoid blocking the front or rear air grilles with equipment, arms, or paperwork.
Work at least several inches inside the sash opening, away from the front edge, to preserve the air barrier.
Decontaminate the work surface before and after use.

Do not use an open flame inside a BSC — flames disrupt the cabinet's airflow pattern and can damage the HEPA filter; use alternatives like a micro-incinerator or disposable loops if flaming is otherwise part of the workflow.
importantSettings: Sash height, kept at the manufacturer-certified operating position — raising it beyond that position compromises the air barrier.
calibration: Requires certification by a qualified technician on a regular schedule (commonly annually or after any relocation/filter change) verifying airflow velocity and HEPA filter integrity.
maintenance: Report any unusual airflow, noise, or alarm to facility safety staff and cease infectious work until resolved.
Keep the interior surfaces decontaminated and free of unnecessary clutter.

commonErrors.cause: Blocked air grilles, sash raised above the certified operating height, or working too close to the front edge
commonErrors.fix: Clear the grilles, keep the sash at its certified height, and work well inside the cabinet

safety: Never use an open flame inside the cabinet.
Never confuse with a laminar flow clean bench — see the BSC vs. Clean Bench concept entry.
